brief: Pasquariello, Goldman's head of hedge fund coverage, says the primary bull trend is intact after a summer that ran cap-weighted S&P +4% and equal-weighted +7% from Memorial Day to Labor Day, while index returns hid a momentum unwind: Goldman's TMT momentum pair printed its worst two months on record and has halved since the June highs. Because the coming stretch is catalyst rich (a possible BOJ 50bp hike, a data-dependent Fed whose decision this week's PPI and pivotal CPI will seal, midterms that typically firm volatility, constrained warfare in the Strait of Hormuz pushing European gas higher) and because implied volatility sits just above YTD lows, his repeated advice is to collect cheap convexity. On direction he expects a choppy near-term path and risk/reward neutral at best given seasonals and supply/demand technicals, then a rally through year-end once midterms pass. House view keeps the Fed on hold. Deficit math has deteriorated without any marked rise in rate volatility. Hedge funds, up 14% fundamental and 17% systematic YTD, offered ballast as bonds lost insurance value. The closing chart: forward P/E over forward margins approaching post-tech-bubble lows, territory last seen in the US and European financial crises.
